newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada buys Canadian dollars for U.S..
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada buys Canadian dollars for U.S..

text.p: The Bank of Canada intervened in the Canadian currency market through brokers, buying Canadian dollars and selling U.S. at around the C$1.3530 level, traders said on Monday.

"I think what they want to do is try to calm the market a little bit because the currency is extremely weak," said one trader. He said some players cited Canada bond coupons coming due at the beginning of December as a reason for the currency's weakness.
The Canada dollar was at C$1.3519 after the intervention.
Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange with CIBC Wood Gundy, said C$1.3530 was an important technical level.
